nodes.name: Emperor Franz Joseph I (+ Empress Elisabeth 'Sisi', r. 1848–1916 CE)
nodes.role: Emperor of Austria & King of Hungary
nodes.notes: Longest-reigning Habsburg monarch of Austria-Hungary; great-uncle of Otto & Karl von Habsburg.

nodes.name: Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria-Este (Nephew of Franz Joseph, 1863–1914 CE)
nodes.notes: His 1914 assassination at Sarajevo triggered World War I.

nodes.notes: Final Austrian Emperor Karl I (grandnephew of Franz Joseph) -> Crown Prince Otto -> Karl von Habsburg (b. 1961).

nodes.notes: House of Savoy sovereign proclaimed first King of Italy in 1861 CE.

nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Almanach de Gotha, Savoy Royal Archives.

nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Almanach de Gotha, Greek Royal Archives.

nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Almanach de Gotha, Greek Royal Archives.

nodes.name: Khan Asparukh (681 CE) → Krum → Tsar St. Boris I of Bulgaria (Baptized 864 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Bulgarian Chronicles, De Administrando Imperio.

nodes.name: Tsar Simeon I the Great of Bulgaria (Preslav Golden Age, r. 893–927 CE)
nodes.notes: Educated in Constantinople; proclaimed Tsar of Bulgarians and Greeks.

nodes.name: Tsars Samuel, Ivan Asen II & Simeon II of Bulgaria (10th c. – 2026 Living Line)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Bulgarian Chronicles, De Administrando Imperio.

nodes.name: Grand Župan Stefan Nemanja → King Stefan the First-Crowned (Serbia, 1166–1228 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Serbian Royal Chronicles, Echard Roman History.

nodes.name: Emperor Stefan Uroš IV Dušan ('Dušan the Mighty', Serbian Empire, 1331–1355 CE)
nodes.notes: Promulgated Dušan's Code and raised the Serbian Archbishopric to a Patriarchate.

nodes.name: Prince St. Lazar Hrebeljanović (Kosovo 1389) & Despot Stefan Lazarević (d. 1427 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Serbian Royal Chronicles, Echard Roman History.

nodes.name: Voivodes Mircea the Elder & Vlad III Drăculea ('Vlad the Impaler', Wallachia, 1386–1476)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Danubian Chronicles, Knolles Turkish History.

nodes.name: Voivode St. Stephen the Great of Moldavia (Ştefan cel Mare, r. 1457–1504 CE)
nodes.notes: Fought 36 battles defending Moldavia; cousin-ally of Vlad III and candidate to Matthias Corvinus.

nodes.name: King Carol I, King Ferdinand I & Queen Marie of Romania (Granddaughter of Queen Victoria, 1866–1938)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Almanach de Gotha.

nodes.name: King Michael I of Romania (+ Anne of Bourbon-Parma) & Margareta (Living 2026)
nodes.role: Final King of Romania & Custodian of the Crown
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Almanach de Gotha.

nodes.name: Empress Dowager Lü Zhi (+ Liu Bang / Han Gaozu; First Woman Ruler of Imperial China, d. 180 BCE)
nodes.notes: Consort of Han founder Liu Bang (Han Gaozu) & regent of Early Western Han.

nodes.name: Emperor Xuan of Han / Liu Bingyi (Great-Grandson of Han Wudi, r. 74–49 BCE)
nodes.notes: Golden Age Western Han sovereign under whom the Xiongnu submitted.

nodes.name: Emperor Wang Mang (Xin Dynasty Interregnum, 9–23 CE)
nodes.notes: Nephew of Empress Wang Zhengjun between Western & Eastern Han.

nodes.name: Emperor Ming of Han & Emperor Zhang (Patron of First Buddhist Temple at Luoyang, 57–88 CE)
nodes.notes: Sons & grandsons of Han Guangwu; sent Ban Chao along the Silk Road.

nodes.name: Emperor Xian of Han / Liu Xie (Final Han Emperor, Abdicated 220 CE to Cao Pi)
nodes.notes: Last Eastern Han monarch whose 220 CE abdication launched the Three Kingdoms.

nodes.name: Emperor Wu of Jin / Sima Yan (Reunified China 280 CE, Western Jin Dynasty)
nodes.notes: Grandson of Sima Yi; ended the Three Kingdoms era in 280 CE.

nodes.name: Emperor Xiaowen of Northern Wei (Tuoba Hong / Yuan Hong, r. 471–499 CE)
nodes.notes: Sinicized Northern Wei court and built the Longmen Grottoes.

nodes.name: Emperor Yang of Sui / Yang Guang (Built Grand Canal, r. 604–618 CE)
nodes.notes: Son of Sui Wendi; completed the Grand Canal before Tang Gaozu's rise.

nodes.name: Emperor Tang Gaozong & Empress Regnant Wu Zetian (Zhou Dynasty, 624–705 CE)
nodes.role: Sole Female Emperor Regnant of China
nodes.notes: Only woman in Chinese history to reign as Huángdì (Emperor Regnant) in her own right; mother of Emperors Zhongzong & Ruizong.

nodes.name: Emperor Suzong → Dezong → Xianzong of Tang (Post-An Lushan Restoration, 756–820 CE)
nodes.notes: Son of Tang Xuanzong; rebuilt Tang authority after An Lushan.

nodes.name: Emperor Taizu Yelü Abaoji (Founder of Khitan Liao Dynasty, 907–926 CE)
nodes.notes: Khitan founder whose western branch formed Qara Khitai.

nodes.name: Emperor Taizu Wanyan Aguda (Founder of Jurchen Jin Dynasty, 1115–1123 CE)
nodes.notes: Jurchen ancestor of the Aisin Gioro / Manchu Qing founders.

nodes.name: Emperors Renzong (Northern Song Peak) & Gaozong (1st Southern Song Emperor, 1022–1162 CE)
nodes.notes: Golden Age Northern Song Renzong & Southern Song founder Gaozong.

nodes.name: Emperors Xuande (Zhu Zhanji) & Zhengtong / Tianshun of Ming (1425–1464 CE)
nodes.notes: Grandson & great-grandson of Emperor Yongle; patronized Zheng He's final voyage.

nodes.name: Emperor Wanli / Zhu Yijun (48-Year Ming Reign, r. 1572–1620 CE; Hosted Matteo Ricci)
nodes.notes: Longest-reigning Ming emperor; sent armies to defend Joseon Korea in the Imjin War.

nodes.name: Emperor Chongzhen / Zhu Youjian (17th & Final Ming Emperor of Beijing, d. 1644 CE)
nodes.notes: Grandson of Wanli; died in 1644 CE as Manchu Qing entered Beijing.

nodes.name: Emperor Yongzheng / Yinzhen (4th Son of Kangxi; Father of Qianlong, r. 1722–1735 CE)
nodes.notes: Son of Kangxi & father of Qianlong.

nodes.name: Qing Emperors Jiaqing, Daoguang, Xianfeng, Tongzhi & Guangxu (1796–1908 CE)
nodes.notes: Late 19th-century Qing emperors ruling under Empress Dowager Cixi prior to Puyi.

nodes.name: Sultans Qutb al-Din Aibak & Shams ad-Din Iltutmish (Founders of Delhi Sultanate, 1206–1236 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Ferishta History of Hindostan, Ibn Battuta.

nodes.name: Sultana Razia al-Din (First & Only Woman Sultan of Delhi, r. 1236–1240 CE)
nodes.notes: Daughter of Sultan Iltutmish designated above her brothers as sovereign ruler of Delhi.

nodes.name: Sultan Alauddin Khalji (Repelled Mongol Invasions, r. 1296–1316 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Ferishta History of Hindostan, Ibn Battuta.

nodes.name: Sultan Muhammad bin Tughluq (Appointed Ibn Battuta Chief Qadi of Delhi, r. 1325–1351 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Ferishta History of Hindostan, Ibn Battuta.

nodes.name: Emperor Sher Shah Suri (Built Grand Trunk Road & Rupee Currency, r. 1540–1545 CE)
nodes.notes: Defeated Humayun and reorganized North Indian administration & currency.

nodes.name: Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah I (Founder of Hyderabad Nizams, 1724–1748 CE)
nodes.notes: Mughal governor under Aurangzeb who founded the Asaf Jahi dynasty.

nodes.name: Sultan Hyder Ali & Tipu Sultan ('Tiger of Mysore', r. 1761–1799 CE)
nodes.notes: Modernizing South Indian sovereigns who allied with France against British rule.

nodes.name: Maharani Lakshmibai of Jhansi (Queen of Jhansi, 1828–1858 CE)
nodes.notes: Born Manikarnika Tambe in a Maratha Peshwa court family; central heroine of 1857.

nodes.name: King Prithvi Narayan Shah (Unifier of Kingdom of Nepal, 1743–1775 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Nepalese Royal Chronicles (Mewar Sisodia Descent).

nodes.name: Kings Tribhuvan, Mahendra, Birendra & Gyanendra of Nepal (Shah Dynasty, 1911–2008 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Nepalese Royal Chronicles (Mewar Sisodia Descent).

nodes.name: Druk Gyalpo Ugyen Wangchuck (1st Hereditary King of Bhutan, r. 1907–1926 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Bhutanese Royal Chronicles.

nodes.name: LIVING (2026): King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck of Bhutan (5th Druk Gyalpo)
nodes.notes: Present-day Dragon King of Bhutan descended from Drukpa Tibetan spiritual-noble houses.

nodes.name: Kings Vajiravudh (Rama VI), Prajadhipok (Rama VII) & Ananda Mahidol (Rama VIII)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Royal Chronicles of Siam & Thailand.

nodes.name: King Bhumibol Adulyadej the Great (Rama IX, r. 1946–2016 CE)
nodes.notes: Reigned 70 years as constitutional monarch of Thailand.

nodes.name: LIVING (2026): King Maha Vajiralongkorn (Rama X) of Thailand
nodes.notes: Present-day reigning Chakri monarch of Thailand (2026).

nodes.name: King Norodom → King Norodom Sihanouk of Cambodia (1834–2012 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Cambodian Royal Chronicles.

nodes.name: LIVING (2026): King Norodom Sihamoni of Cambodia
nodes.notes: Present-day reigning monarch of Cambodia continuing Angkor-Khmer royal heritage.

nodes.name: Sultan Bolkiah (5th Sultan of Brunei, 'Golden Age', r. 1485–1524 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Salasilah Raja-Raja Brunei.

nodes.name: LIVING (2026): Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah of Brunei (29th Sultan, r. 1967–Present)
nodes.notes: One of the longest-reigning monarchs in world history, continuing the Brunei royal line since Muhammad Shah.

nodes.name: LIVING (2026): Sultan Ibrahim of Johor (17th Yang di-Pertuan Agong / King of Malaysia)
nodes.notes: Reigning King of Malaysia (2024–present) from the House of Temenggong / Johor-Malacca continuity.

nodes.name: Imam Muhammad ibn Saud (Founder of First Saudi State at Diriyah, 1744–1765 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Al Saud Najdi Chronicles.

nodes.name: King Abdulaziz ibn Saud (Founder of Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, 1932–1953 CE)
nodes.notes: Unified Nejd and Hejaz into the modern Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

nodes.name: Kings Saud, Faisal, Khalid, Fahd & Abdullah of Saudi Arabia (1953–2015 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Al Saud Najdi Chronicles.

nodes.name: LIVING (2026): King Salman bin Abdulaziz & Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (Saudi Arabia)
nodes.role: Reigning King & Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia (Living 2026)
nodes.notes: Present-day Al Saud monarchs in 2026.

nodes.name: Sultan Said bin Taimur → Sultan Qaboos bin Said of Oman (Al Bu Said, 1932–2020 CE)
nodes.notes: Chronicle succession in Omani Al Bu Said Chronicles.

nodes.name: LIVING (2026): Sultan Haitham bin Tariq of Oman (Al Bu Said Dynasty)
nodes.notes: Cousin of Sultan Qaboos & direct Al Bu Said descendant of Sayyid Said bin Sultan.

nodes.name: Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan (Founder of the United Arab Emirates, 1918–2004 CE)
nodes.notes: Bani Yas Al Nahyan ruler of Abu Dhabi & founding President of the UAE (1971).

nodes.name: LIVING (2026): Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan & Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid (UAE)
nodes.notes: Present-day hereditary rulers of Abu Dhabi & Dubai leading the UAE in 2026.

nodes.name: Sheikh Jassim bin Mohammed Al Thani (Founder of Modern Qatar, c. 1825–1913 CE)
nodes.notes: Mudar-Adnanite Banu Tamim lineage founding Qatar.

nodes.name: LIVING (2026): Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani of Qatar
nodes.notes: Present-day reigning Emir of the State of Qatar.

nodes.name: LIVING (2026): Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad → Emir Mishal al-Ahmad Al-Sabah of Kuwait (Utub)
nodes.notes: Reigning Al-Sabah Emir continuing the 1752 Bani Utbah house of Kuwait.

nodes.name: LIVING (2026): King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa & Crown Prince Salman of Bahrain (Utub)
nodes.notes: Reigning Al Khalifa monarch continuing since 1783 CE.

nodes.name: King Faisal I of Iraq & Syria (3rd Son of Sharif Hussein of Mecca, 1885–1933 CE)
nodes.notes: Brother of King Abdullah I of Jordan; first Hashemite king of Iraq.

nodes.name: Kings Ghazi & Faisal II of Iraq (1912–1958 CE)
nodes.notes: Son & grandson of King Faisal I; cousin to King Hussein of Jordan.

nodes.name: King Antiochus I Theos of Commagene (Nemrut Dağı; Dual Persian-Macedonian Descent, 70–31 BCE)
nodes.notes: Carved colossal twin ancestor galleries tracing his father directly to Darius I and his mother Laodice VII directly to Seleucus & Alexander's world.

nodes.name: Emperor Vaballathus of Palmyra (Son of Queen Zenobia & Odenathus, r. 267–272 CE)
nodes.notes: Co-ruled the Palmyrene Empire with his mother Zenobia.

nodes.name: Mukarrib Karib'il Watar of Saba (Contemporary of Sennacherib, c. 685 BCE)
nodes.notes: Sovereign of South Arabian Saba who exchanged diplomatic gifts with Sennacherib of Assyria.

nodes.name: Queen Gudit / Yodit of Ethiopia (10th c. CE Post-Aksumite Warrior Queen)
nodes.notes: Ended Aksumite era prior to the Zagwe dynasty of Lalibela.

nodes.name: King Evagoras I of Salamis (Cyprus; Teucrid House of Ajax, 411–374 BCE)
nodes.notes: Greek-Cypriot king descended from Teucer (brother of Telamonian Ajax).

nodes.name: Kings Tabnit & Eshmunazar II of Sidon (5th c. BCE Phoenician Royal Sarcophagi)
nodes.notes: Phoenician Sidonian kings granted Dor & Joppa by the Persian Great King.

nodes.name: King Abgar V Ukkama & Queen Helena Contemporary of Edessa / Osroene (r. 4 BCE–50 CE)
nodes.notes: Early Syriac-Armenian ruler of Edessa linked to Adiabene & Armenia.

nodes.name: Satrap-King Mausolus & Queen Artemisia II (+ Queen Ada of Caria; Adoptive Mother of Alexander)
nodes.notes: Builders of the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus; sister Ada adopted Alexander the Great.

nodes.name: Kings Ariarathes I → Ariarathes V of Cappadocia (Persian-Hellenistic Royal Line, 331–130 BCE)
nodes.notes: Cappadocian kings claiming Achaemenid descent and intermarrying with Seleucids & Pontus.

nodes.name: Kings Zipoetes I, Prusias I & Nicomedes IV of Bithynia (326–74 BCE)
nodes.notes: Anatolian Hellenistic kings allied with Macedon, Pontus & Rome.
